faq.q: What is the origin of Hami?
faq.a: Hami is associated with Arabic. Hami is Arabic حَامِي (Ḥāmī) 'protector, defender, one who guards', the active participle of the root ح م ي (ḥ-m-y) 'to protect, to defend'. The source gloss 'support, companion' is close; 'protector, defender' is the lexical sense.
Yes — the underlying form حامي is Arabic.

faq.q: What does Hami mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hami is rendered حامی and carries the sense نگهبان، نگهدارنده.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Hami, hami. Script forms are حامي, حامی, हामी.

faq.q: Is Hami a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
